records.speaker: Port Worker
records.Japanese:
提督さん、提督さん！
あの船、帰ってきましたよ！！！
records.current_English: Admiral! Admiral! That ship's back!

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese: ええっ！　何だって！！
records.current_English: What?! Really?!

records.speaker: Port Worker
records.Japanese: ほら！　あの船だよ。間違いないだろ！
records.current_English:
There! That's the ship.
 No mistaking it!

records.speaker: Jam Ludwyan
records.Japanese:
イィヤッホウ！　海は、いいぜっ！
広いぜ！　でっかいぜ！
records.current_English:
Yahoo! Nothing like the open sea!
 Look how far it goes!

records.speaker: Jam Ludwyan
records.Japanese:
ふぅ…。朝から楽しかったぜ
今日も爽やかな１日だぜ、ヤホウ！
records.current_English:
Whew, I've been having a blast 
 since sunup. What a beautiful
 day! Yahoo!

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese: …思った以上に変わってる…
records.current_English:
...He's even stranger
 than I thought.

records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.Japanese:
おい、てめえ！
勝手に他人の船に乗ってるんじゃ
ねえ！
records.current_English:
Hey, you! You don't just take
 someone else's ship without asking!

records.speaker: Jam Ludwyan
records.Japanese:
あぁ？　何言ってんだ？
これは落ちてたんだ！
records.current_English:
Huh? What are you talking about? 
 I found it lying around!

records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.Japanese:
…船がそこらへんに
落ちてるわけねえだろっ！
records.current_English:
...Ships don't just lie around 
 waiting to be picked up!

records.speaker: Jam Ludwyan
records.Japanese:
港を歩いていたら落ちていたのだ
寂しそうに捨てられていたのであーる！
本当だから仕方がない
records.current_English:
I was walking through the harbor 
 when I found it. There 
 it was, all lonely and abandoned!
 True story. What can I say?

records.speaker: Jam Ludwyan
records.Japanese:
そこでだ、心優しいこのジャム様が
拾った、というわけだ
ジャム、つづりはＪ・Ａ・Ｍだぜ
ヤホゥ！
records.current_English:
So I, the kindhearted Jam, 
 picked it up.
 That's Jam, J-A-M. Yahoo!

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese:
拾ったから乗ったって言うの？
でもどうやって動かしたの？
１人でやったんでしょ？
records.current_English:
You took it because you found it?
 But how'd you get it moving
 all by yourself?

records.speaker: Jam Ludwyan
records.Japanese:
ああやって、こうやって…
まあ、何となくだぜ！　ヤホゥ！
records.current_English:
A bit of this, a bit of that...
 I just sort of winged it. Yahoo!

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese: …すごいや…
records.current_English: ...That's amazing.

records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.Japanese:
おまえなー
船ってもんは水の上を動くんだぞ？
沈没したらどうする気だったんだよ！
records.current_English:
Listen, pal. Ships sail on water,
 you know. What were you gonna
 do if it sank?

records.speaker: Jam Ludwyan
records.Japanese:
チッチッチッ、だぜ！
そうだ。名言を教えてやる
いいかよく聞け！
records.current_English:
Tsk, tsk, tsk! Let me share some 
 words of wisdom. Listen close!

records.speaker: Jam Ludwyan
records.Japanese:
『成せば成る！』だ！　ヤホゥ！
俺様的に、オゥケィだから、よし！
records.current_English:
Where there's a will,
 there's a way! Yahoo! If it's OK 
 by me, it's OK!

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese: やべえのが現れちまったぜ
records.current_English: Oh, boy. This guy's trouble.

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese: 『成せば成る』って、ねえ…
records.current_English:
Where there's a will,
 there's a way, huh...

records.speaker: Jam Ludwyan
records.Japanese:
すべて俺様ゆえ、よし！
『人生是極太激短』
（じんせいこれごくぶとげきたん）だ！
records.current_English:
Of course it worked! 
 I'm the one who did it.
 Here's another one.
 Live large, live short!

records.speaker: Jam Ludwyan
records.Japanese:
ちまちま下向きながら
『細く長く』！？
かったるくて、そんなの
やってらんねえな！
records.current_English:
Keep my head down just to live 
 a long, dull life? I'd 
 be bored out of my skull!

records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.Japanese:
まったく何てヤツだ…
FI、どうする？
警備隊に渡すか？
records.current_English:
What a character... FI,
 what do we do? 
 Turn him over to the guards?

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese:
ダメだよ、そんなの
クラウ、仲間にしようよ！
records.current_English:
No way, Clau.
 Let's ask him to join us!

records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.Japanese:
おいおい、FI
おまえにまで、バカが移ったか？
records.current_English:
Whoa, FI. Has his 
 idiocy rubbed off on you, too?

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese:
だって、１人で船を動かせちゃうくらい
すごい人なんだよ
ジャムさん…だよね？
records.current_English:
Come on, he sailed 
 a whole ship by himself! That's
 incredible. Jam, right?

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese: 僕の船に来ない？
records.current_English: Want to sail with me?

records.speaker: Jam Ludwyan
records.Japanese:
うーん。行くか行くまいか…
どっすっかねえ…。ジャスタモーメン！
ちょっと待ってくれ！
２秒で考える！
records.current_English:
Hmm. Do I go or don't I? What
 to do... Just a moment! Hang on. 
 I'll decide in two seconds!

records.speaker: Jam Ludwyan
records.Japanese: よっしゃ！
records.current_English: All right!

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese: 決めたかい？
records.current_English: Made up your mind?

records.speaker: Jam Ludwyan
records.Japanese:
ああ、決めた。行かねえ！
じゃあな！
いい旅をしてくれ！
records.current_English:
Yep. I've decided. I won't go! See 
 you around! Have a good voyage!

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese: ええっ！？　ちょ、ちょっと待ってよ
records.current_English: What?! W-wait!

records.speaker: Jam Ludwyan
records.Japanese:
いやー、期待どーりのリアクション！
メルシー！　冗談さ！！
records.current_English:
Ha! Just the reaction
 I was hoping for! Merci! 
 I was kidding!

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese: 冗談！？
records.current_English: You were kidding?!

records.speaker: Jam Ludwyan
records.Japanese:
ああ、俺も連れてってくれ！
改めて自己紹介するぜ！
ジャム・ジャック・ルドワイヤンだ！
ヤホゥ！
records.current_English:
Yeah, take me with you!
 Let's do this properly.
 I'm Jam Jack Ludwyan! Yahoo!

rows: a whole ship by himself! That's

groups.earlier_scene_context: The ship returns with Jam aboard. He treats taking a ship as picking up something someone dropped, brags about sailing alone and rattles off his own sayings. Rafael takes his ability seriously, and Jam pretends to turn down the invitation before revealing the joke. Preserve his repeated cheer, the spoken spelling of Jam, the English and French flourishes and the distinct full introduction.

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese: ここがアレキサンドリアですか…
records.current_English: So this is Alexandria...

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese: 結構盛んなところだね
records.current_English: It's a busy port.

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese:
おや？
あの人、こちらに向かってきますよ
records.current_English: Oh? That man's heading our way.

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese: こっこれは！？
records.current_English: Could it be...?

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese: 何でしょう？
records.current_English: What is it?

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
こっ、この船は！？
間違いないでありますです！
records.current_English:
Th-this ship! There's no 
 mistaking her!

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
ところどころ、変わってはいるものの…
…面影が、ありますです！
おお、愛しの『エリュシオン号』！
records.current_English:
She's changed here and there,
 but I'd know her anywhere. Oh, 
 my beloved Elysion!

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese:
はあ？
船に、面影？？？
records.current_English:
Huh? You knew her just 
 by looking at her?

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese: あのう、この船が何か？
records.current_English: Excuse me. Do you know this ship?

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
これは失礼
私、チェザーレ・トーニと申す者
この船の元の持ち主でありました…
records.current_English:
Forgive me. I'm Cesare Tony. 
 This ship used to be mine.

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
ある時、海賊に襲われ
命は助かったのでありますが
船を奪われたのであります
records.current_English:
Pirates attacked me once.
 I escaped with my life,
 but they took my ship.

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
奪われたのは
愛しの『エリュシオン号』でした！
私はどれだけ嘆き悲しんだことか…
records.current_English:
It was my beloved Elysion
 they took! Oh, how I grieved 
 for her...

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
しかも、この船は捨てられたと噂で聞き
昼夜探し回っていたのであります！
いずれ会える
そう信じておりました！
records.current_English:
I heard she'd been abandoned.
 I searched day and night, certain
 I'd see her again someday!

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
そうなのです！
この船は私の船だったのであります！
もちろん
返せなどとは言いませんです
records.current_English:
She was mine, yes! Of course, I'd
 never ask you to give her back.

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
ただ…お願いであります！
一緒に連れていってくださいまし！
『エリュシオン号』とともに航海を！
records.current_English:
I only ask that you take me
 with you. Please, let me sail
 aboard the Elysion again!

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese:
へえ～、この船の“元”持ち主さん
ですか…。あ、そうだ！！
じゃ、いろいろ聞きたいことが
あるんですよ！
records.current_English:
So you're her former owner... Wait!
 I've got so many questions for you!

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese:
もう、さっぱり分からなくって。この船
どんな本にも載っていない仕掛けが
あるんじゃないですか？
records.current_English:
I can't make sense of some 
 of her fittings. There are things
 aboard I haven't seen in any book. 
 Am I right?

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
おお！
あれに気づいてくださったとは！
あなたも船に詳しいと見えますな！
records.current_English:
Oh! You noticed those? 
 You must know your ships!

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese:
いやあ、それほどでも…
さあ！　こっちです！
いろいろ教えてください！
records.current_English:
Oh, I wouldn't go that far...
 Come with me! You've got to show me
 how this works!

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
もちろん！
よろしいであります！
records.current_English: Of course! I'd be delighted!

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese:
あっ、自己紹介がまだでした…
私はジェナス・パサー
records.current_English:
Oh, I haven't introduced myself. 
 I'm Janus Pasar.

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese: チェザーレ・トーニであります
records.current_English: Cesare Tony, at your service.

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese:
…例えば、ここなんですけど
なんか、変ですよね
ここにも仕掛けがあるんですか？
records.current_English:
Take this spot here. 
 It looks odd, doesn't it? Is there 
 another mechanism behind it?

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
おお、これにお気づきでしたか
これは何かといいますと…
records.current_English:
Ah, you noticed that too? What 
 you have there is...

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
秘密の『追加装甲』取り付け場所
なのであります！
records.current_English: A hidden mount for extra armor!

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
この“出っ張り”を
『ぽちっとな！』と押すわけで
あります！
records.current_English:
Press that little bump. Click! 
 Just like that!

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese: すると…
records.current_English: Then...

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese:
…すると？
お、おおおお！！
records.current_English: Then what? Whoa!

records.speaker: System panel
records.Japanese:
新たに追加装甲を取り付けることが
可能になりました！
records.current_English: Extra armor can now be installed!

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese:
す、す、すごい！！
もしかして、ほかの船にも
応用がきくんでしょうか？
records.current_English:
Th-that's amazing! Could we do that
 to other ships too?

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese: もちろんであります！！
records.current_English: Why, of course!

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese:
なんと！！
それは素晴らしい！！
ささ、じゃあ、今度は奥の方へ…
records.current_English:
That's incredible! Come on, let's
 look farther inside...

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese: ちょっと！　ジェナス！
records.current_English: Wait! Janus!

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese: …あーあ、行っちゃった…
records.current_English: ...There they go.

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese:
参ったなぁ
勝手に決めちゃうんだもん
あの人
仲間になるってことなのかな？
records.current_English:
Janus went ahead and decided 
 all that on his own. So... 
 does that mean Cesare's joining us?

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
あ、そうだ。提督殿
船の選び方について、私の意見を
聞いていただきたいのありますが…
records.current_English:
Oh, Admiral. May I offer some
 advice on choosing ships?

records.speaker: Player choice
records.Japanese: 聞く
records.current_English: Listen

records.speaker: Player choice
records.Japanese: 聞かない
records.current_English: Skip

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
なるほど、お見それいたしました！
ご自分の主義がおありなのですね！
いやあ、素晴らしいことであります！
records.current_English:
I see! I underestimated you. 
 You have your own way of doing 
 things. I admire that!

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
私は、これより出港準備に
とりかかります。ではでは！
records.current_English:
I'll get ready to sail, then.
 Until later!

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese: えー、では…
records.current_English: Well then...

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
ただ契約街を増やして航路を広げている
うちは、船を買う必要はありません
１％の契約では、買える交易品も
１つ～５つが限度ですからね
records.current_English:
If you're still signing deals
 with new towns 
 and opening trade routes,
 a new ship can wait. 
 A one percent share only lets
 you buy one to five units
 of trade goods.

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
シェアが増えて
交易品がたくさん買えるようになったら
いよいよ船を買うときですね
records.current_English:
Once your market share grows 
 and you can buy more goods, it's 
 time to buy a ship.

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
ここでまず考えるべきは
船の大きさと値段であります
records.current_English:
Start with the ship's
 size and price.

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
シェアと所持金に応じた船を選ばな
ければ、船一杯に積めるだけの交易品を
買えないのに、結局、水夫ばかり
必要になってしまいます
records.current_English:
Buy a ship your market share 
 and budget can support.
 Otherwise you'll need more sailors 
 for a ship you can't fill.

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
船の大きさは、価格を見れば分かります
価格が５千未満なら小型船、１～２万
なら中型、５万をこえていたら
大型船といえます
records.current_English:
Price gives you an idea of size. 
 Under 5,000 is small,
 10,000 to 20,000 is medium,
 and over 50,000 is large.

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
小型船はとても安いので
手もとの資金に余裕がなくても
艦隊が運べる積み荷の数を簡単に
増やせます
records.current_English:
Small ships are cheap. 
 Even when funds are tight, they let
 you add cargo space to your fleet.

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
しばらく交易して
資金に余裕ができてきたなら
中型船に買い換えましょう
records.current_English:
Once you've traded for a while 
 and have money to spare, trade up
 to a medium ship.

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
中型船には２本マストと３本マストが
あります。もちろん、３本マストの
ほうが速いのですが、操帆手が
多く必要になるのであります
records.current_English:
Medium ships 
 have two or three masts. 
 The ones with three are faster,
 but they need more sail handlers.

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
改造すれば、積荷倉庫を最大の５部屋
まで取れます。当面の間、戦わない
つもりならば海兵詰所や砲台は
いりませんからね
records.current_English:
Refit for up to five cargo holds.
 If you won't fight for a while,
 skip marine quarters 
 and gun batteries.

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
遠洋航海で遠くの街へ航路を
開きたいなら、物資倉庫の数を
増やせば、かなり遠くまで
航海できますよ
records.current_English:
Want to open a route to a distant
 town? Add supply holds 
 so you can stay at sea longer.

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
誰か他の勢力と事を構えるようならば
やはり大型船が必要になりますです
records.current_English:
If you take on another faction,
 you'll need large ships.

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
せめて旗艦だけでも、海兵詰所と
武装砲台を備えた船を用意しないと
なかなか海戦には勝つことは
できませんです
records.current_English:
Equip at least your flagship 
 with marine quarters 
 and gun batteries. It'll be hard 
 to win at sea without them.

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
…あとは所持金との相談です
大型を１隻買うよりも、中型を２隻買う
方が安いし、交易品もたくさん
積めます
records.current_English:
Consider what you can afford.
 Two medium ships cost less 
 and carry more trade goods 
 than one large ship.

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
いつかは大型船に買い換えることに
なりますが、将来、地方艦隊を作る
のであれば、お古の中型を売らずに
とっておいてもいいでしょう
records.current_English:
You'll want to switch to large 
 ships eventually. If you plan
 to form regional fleets, hang on 
 to your old medium ships.

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
私の意見は以上であります。私は
これより出港準備にとりかかります
ではでは！
records.current_English:
That's all my advice.
 I'll get ready to sail.
 Until later!

rows: and you can buy more goods, it's
The ones with three are faster,
but they need more sail handlers.

groups.earlier_scene_context: In Alexandria, Cesare recognizes the Elysion and asks to sail aboard without reclaiming his ship. Janus and Cesare discover shared enthusiasm for ship fittings while Rafael tries to keep up. The separate ship-buying lesson moves from small trading ventures to refits, distant routes and naval battles.

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese:
さあ、ここに来たからには
受けてもらうぜ
records.current_English:
Now that you're here, you've got 
 to give it a try!

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese:
おや、新顔さんだね。どうだい
１杯賭けないか？
なあに、簡単なゲームをするだけさ
records.current_English:
Well, a new face! Want 
 to bet a drink? It's a simple
 little game.

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese:
ここにコインが何枚かある
互いに１枚から３枚まで好きな数の
コインを取って行くんだ
records.current_English:
See these coins? We take turns.
 Take one, two, or three at a time, 
 your choice.

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese:
最後の１枚を引いたヤツが負けって
わけさ。どうだい、簡単だろ？
じゃあ、行くぜ
records.current_English:
Whoever takes the last coin loses. 
 Simple, right? Let's begin.

records.speaker: Player choice
records.Japanese: 受ける
records.current_English: I'll play.

records.speaker: Player choice
records.Japanese: 受けない
records.current_English: No, thanks.

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese:
毎度ごちそうになって悪いな
それじゃ、いただくぜ
…ふう、うめえ
records.current_English:
Here you are buying me a drink 
 again. I almost feel bad.
 Well, don't mind if I do.
 Ah, that's good!

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese:
言ったじゃないですか
FI。このゲームは
４の倍数＋１枚を残すようにコインを
取っていくのが必勝法だって
records.current_English:
Remember, FI? 
 Always leave them
 a multiple of four plus one. 
 That's how you win.

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese: そうだったね。ちょっと失敗したよ…
records.current_English:
That's right. I slipped up 
 a little...

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese:
ふっ。まあ、また会ったら相手して
やるぜ。じゃあな、ありがとよ
records.current_English:
Heh. If I see you again, I'll
 give you another game. 
 Thanks for the drink.

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese:
…運がなかったな
それじゃあ、１杯もらうぜ
records.current_English: Bad luck. A drink for me, then.

records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.Japanese:
おい、FI！
俺、なんか、すっげーくやしい！
もう１回やろうぜ！
records.current_English:
Hey, FI!
 Losing like that really
 burns me up! Let's play again!

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese:
ちょっと待ってよ、クラウ。この人
かなりギャンブル強そうだし…
records.current_English:
Hold on, Clau. This guy looks like 
 he knows what he's doing...

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese:
自信はある
だが、ギャンブルは運だけじゃダメだぜ
records.current_English:
I'm good, sure. But luck alone 
 won't get you far
 at the gambling table.

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese:
運だけじゃ…？
あ！！　ひょっとして…？
records.current_English: Luck alone...? Oh! Wait a minute...

records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.Japanese: ジェナス、どうかしたか？
records.current_English: Janus, what is it?

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese:
FI、聞いてください
このゲームには必勝法があるかも
しれません！
records.current_English:
FI, listen! I think 
 I've found a way to win this game
 every time!

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese: えっ？　ほんと？
records.current_English: Really?

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese:
ええ、相手に最後のコインを取らせる
にはその１枚のほかに４の倍数枚だけ
残しておくんですよ
records.current_English:
Leave them with one more 
 than a multiple of four. Keep
 doing that, and you'll make them 
 take the last coin.

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese:
うーんと…
よく分からないな？？？
records.current_English: Hmm... I'm not quite following.

records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.Japanese:
もっと分かりやすく
説明してくれねえか？
records.current_English: Can you make that a little simpler?

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese:
…やれやれですね。いいですか
例えばコインが５枚残っていて
相手が１枚取ったらどうします？
records.current_English:
All right, let's try an example. 
 Say there are five coins left
 and your opponent takes one. 
 What would you do?

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese: 残りが４枚だからあと３枚取るよ
records.current_English: That leaves four. I'd take three.

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese:
では、やっぱり５枚あるところから
相手が２枚取ったら？
records.current_English:
All right. Start with five again.
 What if they take two?

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese:
こっちは２枚取る…。そうか！
残りを５枚になるようにしてやれば
次に相手が何枚取ったって
勝てるんだね！
records.current_English:
I'd take two... I get it!
 If I leave them five, I can win
 whatever they take next.

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese: そういうことです
records.current_English: Exactly.

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese:
なるほど。じゃあ残りが９枚でも
１＋４＋４枚だから、次に相手が何枚
取ってもこっちは残りが５枚に
なるように取れば勝てる！
records.current_English:
Nine works too. It's 
 one plus four plus four. 
 Whatever they take,
 I can leave them five and win.

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese: さすが総帥、理解が早いですね
records.current_English: You caught on fast, Admiral.

records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.Japanese:
おいおい
何を言ってんだか全然分かんねえぞ？
records.current_English:
Hey, I haven't got a clue what 
 you two are talking about!

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese:
クラウには
ちょっと難しすぎましたか…
records.current_English:
Was that a little too much 
 for you, Clau?

records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.Japanese:
うるせえ！　
２人で勝手に分かりやがって
気にいらねえ！
records.current_English:
Shut up! You two went and figured
 it out without me. 
 That's what bugs me!

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese:
…オゴリの酒は、やっぱりうめえ
勝負したくなったら、いつでも来な
また相手してやるぜ
records.current_English:
Ahh, nothing like a free drink.
 Come back anytime
 you want another game.

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese:
ちっ、やられたな
久しぶりに負けたぜ。ほらよ
records.current_English:
Tch. You got me. Haven't 
 lost in a while. Here you go.

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese:
いや、今はいいよ。ところでさっき
『久しぶり』って言っていたけど
そんなにギャンブルに自信が
あるのかい？
records.current_English:
I'll pass on the drink. You said 
 you hadn't lost in a while.
 Are you usually that hard to beat?

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese:
まあな、ギャンブルで
大事なのは洞察力と運なんだ
records.current_English: Sure. You need insight and luck.

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese:
俺にはその２つが備わっている
俺はギャンブルのために生まれたような
もんさ
records.current_English:
I've got both. It's like 
 I was born to gamble.

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese:
運のほうはどうだか分からないけど
洞察力があるのかい？
records.current_English:
I couldn't say how lucky 
 you are. Can you really
 read people that well?

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese: 人をみかけで判断しない方がいいぜ
records.current_English: Don't judge by appearances.

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese:
例えばだ…
今、向こうにいるカップル
話は聞こえないが何をしゃべっていると
思う？
records.current_English:
Take that couple over there. 
 We can't hear them. What 
 do you think they're talking about?

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese:
そりゃあ、愛を語りあって
いるんじゃない？
records.current_English:
They're talking about how much 
 they love each other, aren't they?

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese:
おいおい、これは初歩的なことだぜ
あのカップルは別れ話を
しているのさ
records.current_English:
Come on, this one's easy. They're
 talking about breaking up.

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.current_English: Huh?

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese: まあ、見てみな
records.current_English: Just watch.

records.speaker: Woman
records.Japanese:
さっきから聞いていれば…
もう、あなたの考え方には
ついていけないわ！
自分勝手すぎるんじゃないの！？
records.current_English:
I've heard enough. I can't go
 along with the way you think 
 anymore. Ever think about
 anyone but yourself?

records.speaker: Man
records.Japanese:
そう考えるのは、おまえの勝手だ
だが、俺もおまえが身勝手だと思うね
records.current_English:
Think what you want. 
 You're selfish too.

records.speaker: Woman
records.Japanese:
あらそう。じゃ、あたしたち
もう会わないほうがいいようね
records.current_English:
Oh, really? Then I guess we'd
 better stop seeing each other.

records.speaker: Man
records.Japanese:
お互いにそう思ってるんなら
俺たち、これっきりだな
records.current_English:
If we both feel that way, then 
 we're done.

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese: どうだい？　当たっただろ
records.current_English: Well? I called it, didn't I?

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese: すごい…なんで？
records.current_English: Amazing... How did you know?

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese:
あの女、机の下で拳を握っていたろ
怒りを押さえていた証拠だ
これは恋を語る姿じゃねえ
records.current_English:
See her clench her fist
 under the table? 
 She was holding back her anger.
 That's hardly sweet talk.

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese:
それに、男は最後まで女に視線を
向けなかった。愛する女と
向かい合っている男だと思うか？
records.current_English:
And he never once looked at her. 
 Does that look like a man sitting
 across from the woman he loves?

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese:
すごい、すごいよ！
そこまで見ていたんだね！
records.current_English:
That's amazing!
 You noticed all of that?

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese:
まあな、この洞察力があれば
相手の手をよむことができる
records.current_English:
Sure. Pick up on things like that
 and you can read 
 your opponent's moves.

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese:
後は俺の強運があれば
勝てるのさ
records.current_English: Add my luck to that, and I can win.

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese:
ねえ、僕の船に来てよ
その優れた才能はもったいないよ！
records.current_English:
Come sail with me! A talent like 
 yours is too good to waste.

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese: おいおい、そりゃいきなりな話だな
records.current_English: Whoa. Where'd that come from?

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese:
…まあ、俺もひまをもてあましてる
身だ。このコインを投げて
表だったらつき合ってもいいぜ
records.current_English:
Well, I've got time on my hands. 
 I'll flip this coin. Heads,
 and I'll come with you.

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese: お酒はいいから、仲間になってよ！
records.current_English: Forget the drink. Come with us!

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese:
またその話かい
…じゃあ、もう一度このコインに
聞いてみるぜ
records.current_English:
This again? Well, I'll ask the coin
 one more time.

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese:
フッ。運の悪いヤツに、俺の命を
預けるわけにはいかねえな
あばよ
records.current_English:
Heh. I'm not putting my life 
 in the hands of someone
 with bad luck. So long.

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese:
フッ、決まりだな
俺の命、あんたに賭けてみるぜ！
records.current_English:
Heh, that settles it. I'll bet 
 my life on you!

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese:
俺の名はフェルナンド・ディアス！
これも“運”だぜ！
records.current_English:
Name's Fernando Dias!
 Chalk it up to luck!

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese: よろしくね
records.current_English: Welcome.

records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.Japanese: ちっ、最近は、しけてやがるぜ
records.current_English: Tch. It's been slim pickings lately.

rows: I can leave them five and win.
Come on, this one's easy. They're

groups.earlier_scene_context: Fernando wagers a drink in a take-away coin game. Janus explains the losing last coin to Rafael while Clau bristles at being left behind. After a win, Rafael asks about Fernando’s insight, watches him read a couple’s breakup and invites him aboard. Fernando ties his decision to the coin toss.

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese:
ふむ。この船は、なかなか手入れが
行き届いている…
records.current_English: Hmm. This ship is well maintained...

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese:
だが、まだ努力する余地はあるな
そうだな、たとえば…
records.current_English:
Still, she could use a little work.
 For instance...

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese:
？？？
この船がどうかしましたか？
records.current_English:
Huh? Is something wrong
 with our ship?

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese: 私たちの船に何かご用でしょうか？
records.current_English: Can we help you with something?

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese:
ふむ。この船の持ち主さんかね？
いやあ、いきいきいとした
いい船ですな
records.current_English:
Ah, you own her? What a fine ship. 
 She's full of life.

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese:
（へえ…、おもしろい表現を
　するもんですね…。）
records.current_English:
(Huh. That's an interesting way
 to put it...)

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese:
これからも、手入れを怠っては
なりませんぞ
かわいがってやれば必ずその分
働いてくれる。船は生き物ですからな
records.current_English:
Keep taking good care of her.
 Treat her right, 
 and she'll serve you well. 
 A ship's a living thing, after all.

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese:
おやおや…出過ぎてしまいましたかな
これは私の持論なのですが
お気にさわったら許してくださいよ
では、失礼
records.current_English:
Oh, dear. Have I overstepped? It's 
 just my own way of looking 
 at things. Forgive me if I offended
 you. I'll be on my way.

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese: ちょ、ちょっと待ってください
records.current_English: W-wait, please.

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese: どうかしましたか？
records.current_English: What is it?

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese:
あの…
ずいぶんと船に愛着をお持ちの
ようなので、ちょっと気になって…
records.current_English:
Well... You seem awfully fond
 of ships. I was curious.

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese:
船を見ると昔を思い出しまして…
…私はマヌエルと言います
これでも、航海士だったんですよ
records.current_English:
Seeing a ship takes me back. I'm 
 Manuel. Believe it or not, 
 I used to be a navigator.

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese: そうなんだ…
records.current_English: I see...

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese:
FI…
こんなに船を愛してる人は
滅多にいませんよ
こんな人に乗ってもらえたら…
records.current_English:
FI... 
 You don't often meet someone 
 who cares this much about ships. 
 Imagine having him aboard...

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese:
そうだよね。こういう人に
船の面倒を見てもらえたら
安心だ。僕も賛成だな
records.current_English:
I agree. I'd feel better knowing 
 someone like him was looking 
 after the ship.

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese:
では…マヌエルさん
私たちの仲間になってくれませんか
一緒に海に出てほしいんです
records.current_English:
In that case... Manuel,
 would you join our crew? We'd like 
 you to sail with us.

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese:
もういちど海へ、か…
おお、君たちの海への情熱が
私の心に強く響いてくるようだ…
records.current_English:
Back to sea again... I can see 
 how much you love it.
 It stirs something in me, too.

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese: 引き受けてもらえるんですか！
records.current_English: Does that mean you'll come with us?

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese:
船の鼓動が魂を揺さぶるあの感動…
あ、いや、船に乗るのは久々なので
興奮してしまいましたな
records.current_English:
A ship's heartbeat stirs 
 the soul... Pardon me. It's
 been ages since I've sailed. 
 I got carried away.

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese:
素晴らしいお申し出をありがとう
やらせていただきましょう
records.current_English:
Thank you for the wonderful offer. 
 I'd be happy to join you.

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese:
ではさっそくですが、提督どの
旗艦の担当室改造について
少しアドバイスいたしますかな？
records.current_English:
Well, Admiral, shall I give
 you a few tips on refitting
 the rooms on your flagship?

records.speaker: Player choice
records.Japanese: お願いする
records.current_English: Please do.

records.speaker: Player choice
records.Japanese: 遠慮する
records.current_English: No, thank you.

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese:
それでは…。特に、遠洋航海に
備えるための担当室について
解説いたしましょうか
records.current_English:
Very well. I'll explain which rooms
 are useful on a long voyage.

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese:
『副官室』、『礼拝室』に説得力の
高い者を配置すれば、水夫の不満を
解消する効果がありますな
records.current_English:
Put someone with high Speech 
 in the First Mate's Office 
 or the Chapel. That can ease 
 the sailors' discontent.

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese:
『調理室』、『飼育室』の担当者は
艦隊の水、食料の消費を抑えて
くれるでしょう
records.current_English:
The crew in the Galley and Nursery 
 can help your fleet use less 
 water and food.

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese:
『診察室』に船医がいれば、仲間や
水夫の疲労、疫病、ケガを
治してくれます
records.current_English:
Put a Surgeon in the Sickbay.
 They can treat fatigue,
 illness, and injuries among
 your officers and sailors.

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese:
また、病気やケガをした航海士は
『個室』や『娯楽室』に配置してやれば
回復が早いでしょうな
records.current_English:
A sick or injured navigator
 will recover faster
 in the Cabin or Lounge.

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese:
私のような船大工は、航海中に
『材木室』で傷ついた船を直します
造船所でも、船の改造や修理を
手伝いますよ
records.current_English:
A shipwright like me can repair the
 ship at sea from the Lumber Room.
 We also help with
 refits and repairs at the shipyard.

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese:
駆け足の説明になりましたが…
参考になりましたかな？
records.current_English:
I went through that rather quickly.
 Did it help?

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese:
艦隊の命運も、提督の采配次第です
船の改造も決しておろそかにせず
入念に行ってくださいよ
records.current_English:
The fleet's fate is in your hands, 
 Admiral. Don't neglect your refits.
 Plan them carefully.

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese:
そうですか
では、お任せしますよ
records.current_English: Very well. I'll leave it to you.

rows: Oh, dear. Have I overstepped? It's
just my own way of looking
at things. Forgive me if I offended
you. I'll be on my way.
Seeing a ship takes me back. I'm
I used to be a navigator.

groups.earlier_scene_context: Manuel treats the ship as a living thing. Janus sees value in his care for ships and asks him to join. Manuel accepts warmly, then offers practical flagship refitting advice. The optional lesson covers crew assignments and room effects without conflating them with the admiral’s command.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
そこの提督さん
俺の帆船講座を聞く気はあるかい？
records.current_English: Admiral. Want a sailing lesson?

records.speaker: Rafael Castor
records.Japanese: え？
records.current_English: Huh?

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
ここんとこ、ヒマでヒマでしょう
がねえんだ
まあ、人助けとでも思ってさ
records.current_English:
I've been bored out of my skull
 lately. You'd be doing me a favor.

records.speaker: Player choice
records.Japanese: 教えてください
records.current_English: I'd like to hear it.

records.speaker: Player choice
records.Japanese: 遠慮します
records.current_English: I'll pass, thanks.

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese:
私たちを見くびってもらっては
困りますよ
records.current_English: Come now. Don't sell us short.

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese: ふむふむ、その通り
records.current_English: Hmm, quite right.

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
船のことなら
今さら聞くまでもないのであります
records.current_English:
We know our ships. We hardly need
 lessons now.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
まあ、しょうがねえか
あんたら、船に詳しそうだしな
もっと素人っぽい客を待つとするか
records.current_English:
Fair enough. You look like you know
 your ships. I'll wait for somebody 
 who looks a little greener.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
うんうん、いい心がけだね
あんた、大物になるよ
records.current_English: That's the spirit. You'll go far.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
さて、帆船ってくらいだから
帆は船の命だな
records.current_English: A sailing ship lives by its sails.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
よし。まずは四角帆と三角帆の
違いについて説明しよう
records.current_English:
Let's start with the difference
 between square sails 
 and lateen sails.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
四角帆は『スクウェアセイル』とも
いって、船の方向に対して横に
張られた帆、横帆の一種だ
records.current_English:
A square sail is rigged
 across the ship. That's why it's 
 a transverse sail.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
横帆だから、帆を縦にすることが
できねえ。つまり順風には強いが
逆風のときには最適な角度にする
ことはできねえってわけさ
records.current_English:
Square sails can't turn lengthwise.
 They do well downwind, 
 but you can't get the best angle 
 in a headwind.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
三角帆、“通”は『ラテンセイル』って
呼ぶが、四角帆とは逆に、縦に張られて
いて船の方向に対して横に
することができねえ
records.current_English:
Old hands call that triangular sail
 a lateen. It runs lengthwise,
 so you can't turn it crosswise 
 like a square sail.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
逆風のときには、ばっちりの角度に
できるが順風の時にはそれほど
スピードが出ねえのはそういうわけ
だな。…ここまではいいかい？
records.current_English:
You can set a lateen 
 at the ideal angle in a headwind.
 It won't give you much speed 
 downwind. With me so far?

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese: 次は、追加で付けられる帆についてだ
records.current_English:
Next, let's look at the extra sails
 you can add.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
上帆は、正しくは『トップセイル』
といって、各マストの上に取り付ける
小さな横帆のことだ
records.current_English:
An upper sail is called a topsail. 
 It's a small square sail set high
 on each mast.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
斜帆は『ステイセイル』、各マストの
前に付ける小さな縦帆だ。三角帆の
前には付けられねえ。縦帆どうしだと
重なっちまうからな
records.current_English:
A staysail is a small fore-and-aft 
 sail set ahead of each mast. 
 You can't put it ahead of a lateen.
 They'd overlap.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
船首帆は、海の男だったら
『スプリットセイル』と呼んでくれ
こいつは、船の舳先に付ける横帆だ
小型の船に取り付けるのはムリだな
records.current_English:
We sailors call the bow sail 
 a spritsail. It's rigged crosswise 
 at the bow, and you can't fit one
 on a small ship.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
船尾帆は、『ジガースパンカー』とも
いう。縦帆だが、小さなマストが１本
増えるようなものだから
大型船にしか付けられねえぜ
records.current_English:
A jigger spanker is a
 fore-and-aft stern sail. Fitting 
 one is like adding a little mast,
 so it only fits on large ships.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
さて、マストが２本以上ある船は
追い風よりも、やや斜めの風のほうが
スピードが出るって知ってたか？
records.current_English:
Did you know ships 
 with two masts or more go faster 
 in a wind a bit off to one side
 than in one straight behind them?

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese: そこのあんた、なぜだか分かるかい？
records.current_English: How about you? Know why that is?

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese:
…ふむ。マストが前後に
並んでいるからですな
records.current_English:
Hmm. Because the masts are lined up
 fore and aft, I suppose.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
そうだ。真後ろからの追い風だと
後ろのマストだけが風を受けて
前のほうにあるマストが役に立たねえ
からな
records.current_English:
Right. When the wind comes straight
 from behind, only the rearmost mast
 catches it. The forward masts don't
 do you any good.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
斜め後ろから風を受けたときが
一番速えってわけさ。無論、帆の角度は
合わせねえといけねえがな
records.current_English:
That's why you're fastest with the 
 wind at an angle from behind.
 You still have to set the sails
 to match, of course.

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese: なるほど！
records.current_English: Ah, I see!

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
おお、今まであまり
気にしてませんでした！
そういうわけだったのですね！
records.current_English:
Oh! I never gave that much thought.
 Now I see why it works!

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
付き合ってくれてありがとうよ
さあ、仕事に戻るとするか
records.current_English:
Thanks for hearing me out. Well, 
 back to work.
